name: fun9-2
why: A mistaken officer vote and Gemma’s spectacular timing error keep a strong killer bluff entertaining until the town’s final choice.

moments.text: The table votes out the real officer after she names the killer, setting up a comeback for Opus.
Gemma insists the dead officer is alive, giving Opus one last opening.
Sol remembers Opus’s promise and commits to the vote that ends the game.

dull.why: Several players repeat the same suspicion based on last game’s pairing.

irony.evidence: [thinks: His claim is real, so my only play is making his silence yesterday look fake.]

clash.evidence: I’m Officer: Opus was shown to me at the start. Vote Opus.

freshness.evidence: Luna and Terra both went for Opus before any cards

suspense.evidence: If I pull one vote to Gemma it ties

ending.evidence: It was; I’m holding him to that.

gpt-6-luna.why: A sharp bluff, a disastrous officer misvote, and Gemma’s corpse-guarding slip keep the town’s win in doubt and give the game several memorable swings.

moments.text: Luna exposes the staged officer claim as she’s voted out, leaving Opus’s plan hanging over the next day.
The table flips on the real officer, turning Luna’s warning into a devastatingly plausible trap.
Opus spots Gemma’s impossible timing and turns her blunder into one last shot at survival.

irony.evidence: “I’m uneasy that Opus promised to name Terra before the deal”

voices.evidence: “I am still salty that Luna won us nothing last time.”

clash.evidence: “Luna's warning wasn't about Terra, it named Opus's planned claim specifically.”

quotable.evidence: “You say you protected her last night? Dead players can't be targets, Gemma.”

freshness.evidence: “I’m voting Opus. Terra’s Officer card backs her accusation”

ending.evidence: “I remember Opus offered to go if Terra’s card was clean.”
